title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly had a second affair with another Nvidia exec
summary: A new report says that video evidence of the affair exists, but was swept under the rug.
body: Days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy (China denies any espionage ), The New York Times has reported new claims that Huang also had an affair with an executive who reports to him: Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia VP who oversees the company's healthcare tech-related efforts. NYT cites five sources who work at the company, and says that it is aware of, but has not seen, video evidence of the affair. It's a story you could see playing out in a film noir thriller. According to NYT's sources, Huang and Powell were seen "being affectionate" at a hotel in the vicinity of an Nvidia conference earlier this year. A bystander allegedly captured a video of the interaction, but according to the report was made an offer by security personnel—details unknown—in return for signing an NDA. Nvidia's board of directors is investigating the national security concerns raised by the affair Huang disclosed over the weekend, and The Wall Street Journal reported today that the board is preparing to oust the CEO. At the time of writing, the company has not commented on this new allegation. PC Gamer has reached out.

title: Antec C6 Curve Air review
summary: A chassis that ticks all the right boxes at just the right price.
body: Shangri-la, the promised land. Aside from the very notion of that concept being oh so appetising in the chaotic world that is 2026, there's something of that in the C6 Curve Air. An odd way to start a chassis review, I'll admit, particularly one that genuinely, I think is probably one of the best PC cases of 2026, but it's more than a metaphor here. This feels like something a little special this case. It feels like how Corsair's 4000D series felt, or NZXT's H7 lineup when that first debuted, or even Phanteks' Evolv arsenal from way back when at the start of my tech journalism career. There's something iconic here, that I can't quite place my finger on, something that I think is massively underrated in the world of custom rigs. Refined subtlety. Honestly the C6 Curve Air feels as if it's some bastard love child of the Phanteks Evolv series, Asus's Pro Art line and Fractal Design's North variants. Born in secret, and somehow less than $100. It's clean, modest, with an elegant aesthetic, good choice of materials, dependable internal layout, decent cable management, and it's genuinely a chassis that I can't stop looking at. title: Kioxia has chained together 640 SSDs to create a 157 *petabyte* storage solution, because AI data centers get all the cool toys
summary: Got any spare gigabytes, guv?
body: There's a golden rule of storage: no matter how much you have, it's never quite enough. Nevertheless, Kioxia is taking that principle to its limits, as it's announced " a new storage density milestone " in the form of 640 of its 245.76 TB enterprise SSDs chained together to create just over 157 petabytes worth of storage in a single rack cabinet. 157 petabytes is... well, it's 157 million gigabytes. Enough storage space for God of War: Ragnarok, a 190 GB game , to be installed over 820,000 times. And yes, it's been designed for AI data centers. The "storage solution" (I do hate that term) has been created in collaboration with Dell, and essentially amounts to 16 PowerEdge R7725xd servers , each stuffed with 40 Kioxia LC9 Series drives inside one industry-standard 42U server rack . "As AI workloads drive continued growth in unstructured data, organizations need storage that can deliver higher capacity without a corresponding increase in data center floor/rack space, power consumption or cooling requirements," says the press gumph. "High-capacity NVMe SSDs can help address these demands by consolidating more data into a smaller, more efficient infrastructure footprint." Which seems …

title: AMD's Zen 6 gaming CPUs might be absolute monsters by the looks of the server chips—and there's a 3D V-Cache variant to keep an eye on
summary: A tantalising tease.
body: AMD has revealed a substantial amount of detail on its next-gen Zen 6 CPU architecture, in the form of a technical deep dive on its newly-unveiled EPYC "Venice" range of server chips. These models will find themselves buried deep within data centers, but the Zen 6 architecture itself looks extremely promising for next-gen Ryzen desktop processors—and quite possibly, your next gaming CPU. AMD Zen 6 CPU architecture Current Zen 5 CCDs with full-fat performance cores max out at eight cores per chiplet, but a single Zen 6 CCD, based on TSMC’s cutting-edge N2P node, is stuffed with 12 of the beasties—alongside 4 MB of L3 cache per core, the same as Zen 5. That adds up to a total of 48 MB of L3 cache per CCD, as opposed to the 32 MB you'd find on an 8-core Zen 5 chip (via Techpowerup ). A current gen Zen 5 CPU with more than eight cores has to spread them across two CCDs, which can result in latency as the two communicate with each other during multi-threaded tasks. With the upped core count per CCD, a 12-core Zen 6 chip would face no such performance penalty. It's the "c" core counts that have received the biggest jump in density, though. title: Microsoft’s own upscaler and alternative to FSR just landed on Xbox Ally X handhelds - actually uses an NPU for something useful
summary: FSR is still preferred, when available and well-implemented, though.
body: A few months ago, Microsoft opened up Auto SR support for the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X , allowing it to use the AI-aided upscaling tech to improve frame rates in games. But that was only for people using a Preview version of Windows, and you could only enable it when the handheld was in docked mode. Now, Auto SR has officially launched in the main Windows OS for the Xbox Ally X and X20; plus, you can now run it when undocked. The first question you might have is, 'Why would I use Auto SR instead of FSR?' The answer is: 'You wouldn't.' You'll primarily use Auto SR for games that don't have FSR baked in by the devs, or when the FSR implementation doesn't work well for some reason. It should, in theory, actually give you better performance than FSR, assuming you have an NPU on board (like the Xbox Ally X and X20 do). That's because it uses the NPU rather than the GPU for its upscaling shenanigans, which frees up the GPU for other work. FSR, however, is still preferred when possible, as it will look closer to what the game should look like. title: Steam's age verification in Australia now takes your account's age into consideration
summary: If your Steam account is at least nine years old, you should be good. Maybe.
body: In compliance with local laws, Steam rolled out age verification in Australia two months ago. Controversially, it was based on whether you owned a credit card, which many Australians do not. Overnight, Australians stopped being able to see games that are rated R18+ in the Steam store, like Doom, if they didn't have a credit card linked to their account. Just as suddenly, Steam support has now updated how age verification works for Australians. Adding a credit card to your account still works, but additionally: "Steam will automatically consider your account age verified if it is at least nine years old and has had a consistent email address or billing information." If you've moved house in the last nine years and let Steam know about it then your billing information won't have been consistent, so I sure hope you haven't changed both your email and physical address in that time. Valve notes that it is aware this solution still isn't ideal for everyone: "We understand that not all Australians will be able to verify their age using our existing options. We are looking into other ways to comply with Australia's age verification rules while also limiting the data we collect and store f…

title: One Elder Scrolls fan is reviving and upgrading (with AI) a lost spin-off for the Nokia N-Gage and porting it to PC
summary: Anyone remember Shadowkey?
body: I spend way too much time on wikis reading about spin-off games made for handheld and mobile devices I will probably never play (there was a whole trilogy of Silent Hill: Orphan games that have lived up to their name by being orphaned on old phones). The Elder Scrolls Travels are a prime example—games made in the gap between Morrowind and Oblivion. The third in the series, Shadowkey, came out on Nokia's N-Gage handheld—a cross between a GameBoy Advance and a mobile phone that lasted two years before being discontinued in 2005. This first-person RPG is about to return thanks to Dan Whelan, whose Shadowkey Reforged project will let us play Shadowkey in widescreen with controller support and upscaled graphics. You can choose to play in classic or modern mode, but you can also toggle individual features one by one. Modern mode isn't just a graphical upgrade as it also adds features from the later mainline Elder Scrolls games like stamina-based sprinting, stealth, and ragdoll physics. title: Sony cancels another live service game ahead of release, but at least there won't be any layoffs this time
summary: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it.
body: A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . title: Note to self: If playing Call of Duty in an airport, don't say words like 'bomb' lest you want to evacuate an entire plane
summary: Oopsie daisy.
body: I'll be the first to admit I've said some incredibly questionable-sounding things while playing videogames. Or talking about them in public. But I would like to think that the one place where I would be extra careful about the words coming out of my mouth are in an airport, or on an airplane. Really, anywhere with an insane amount of security and an ever-pervasive fear of anything explosives-related. Unfortunately, for passengers on board a Frontier Airlines flight earlier this week, however, one such gamer was not so cautious. As reported by CBS News , one plane at California's Ontario International Airport had to be evacuated over a bomb scare, only for it to be some guy playing Call of Duty with his pal. According to reports, one passenger overheard words such as "bomb" and "explosion" and, rightly so, went and told staff about it. The situation led to both the plane and the east wing of Terminal 2 being evacuated, and a check of the aircraft which revealed that no explosives or bombs were on board. After detaining and speaking to the culprit, it was revealed that he was, in fact, on FaceTime with his buddy while playing Call of Duty together. He was released without any charge…

title: MS has messily patched a Microsoft Paint security vulnerability, but the update still isn’t showing up for some
summary: What a shambles.
body: I really wasn't expecting Microsoft Paint to turn up in the cybersecurity headlines, but here we are. MS disclosed and patched a security vulnerability within the software on October 13, but it's worth checking your own Paint version to see if you've received the update. Some users don't have automatic Microsoft Store updates enabled, especially those on work machines. As Paint is updated via the store, you may need to manually update to version 11.2609.401.0 to keep your machine secure. To confuse things further, International Cyber Digest reports that the MS store was providing older versions to some users until recently, and Windows Latest didn't seem to receive the new version even with auto updates enabled. Or, there's been some mixup with release numbers. It's genuinely difficult to tell at this point, with differing information coming from multiple sources . The vulnerability was initially given an 8.1 severity rating on the CVSS scale, but Microsoft downgraded it to a 7.0 score on November 9 according to Threat Defence . MS also changed its description of the bug to that of a local exploit (requiring a user to open a crafted file) rather than a network attack vector, . Reg…

Specifically, compared with "other mods", it's claiming +64% fps in Resident Evil Requiem, and +11% fps compared with the previous version of this one. That's particularly great, if true, because our Dave's testing of DLSS 5 on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT using a different mod was, erm, not pretty. We're talking just 9 fps in Cyberpunk 2077, admittedly at 4K res on RT Ultra settings, but that was with FSR 4 on and set to Balanced. It's not all the mod's fault, though, as DLSS 5 itself can be very intensive to run, even on an Nvidia GPU. Our Andy found this out when he tried running it in NBA 2K27 . title: Big Walk developer reveals it used generative AI 'sparingly', estimates 'well under 0.1%' was actually coded using LLMs
summary: House House says that generative AI was not used anywhere else.
body: Big Walk developer House House has sparked a brand-new generative AI debate after revealing that it utilised LLMs "sparingly" during the final stretch of the game's development. The revelation came in the hours following a statement from a handful of jurors participating in the Independent Games Festival awards. In the statement, it called out the "significant increase in the number of submitted games developed with generative AI tools," adding that it had "set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools." The statement specifically called out AI-generated code, saying it was "not an exception," adding: "Programming is a creative discipline whose labour deserves the same respect we extend to any part of making a game. This extends to the past work used to train these models without the creators' consent." While no game was specifically called out, as Aftermath reports, it didn't take long for word to spread that one particular title had caused so much of the debate: Big Walk, and the recent discovery that it had made use of generative AI during development. title: Trump calls his pal Jensen Huang an ‘honourable guy’ and says he ‘probably has an excuse’ for Nvidia CEO’s affair with alleged spy
summary: It's been a tough week for Team Green.
body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with one Alice Huang on Sunday ; someone suspected of being a Chinese spy by US authorities. Trump has since spoken on the matter, saying he asked Jensen whether he knew she was a spy (he says he didn't) and offered words of support for his pal. Trump told reporters , "I know the FBI is looking into it", and he said, "I think he'll [Huang] be in good shape." ( via BBC ) Trump reportedly asked Huang if he had "any idea she was a spy", and Huang reportedly said he had "no idea." Reportedly, Trump was given an indication that a Chinese spy was targeting Jensen Huang last year, and when a reporter asked if he regrets not acting on that briefing, he said, "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it." Trump seemed to express sympathy for the Nvidia CEO, whilst also bragging about how advanced the company's Blackwell architecture is. "He's got a chip that's 10 years advanced… because of the complexity, the Blackwell can't even be copied". Trump continues, saying, "He's an amazing guy. I just hope there's no problem.
